items.title: Divergent nitrous oxide accounting can distort crop carbon intensity scores and agricultural trade
items.abstract: Methods for estimating nitrous oxide emissions, a major contributor to the carbon intensity of nitrogen fertilizer-dependent crops, can produce substantially different results across frameworks. Standardized approaches are needed to avoid distorting trade and strengthen incentives for mitigation of emissions.

items.title: Wheat resilience under compound stress
items.abstract: Compound hot–dry–windy events are becoming more frequent and increasingly damaging to wheat yields in China’s wheat belt, underscoring the need for improved crop management, breeding and climate adaptation.

items.title: Wheat yield sensitivity to compound hot–dry–windy events is increasing in China
items.abstract: Increasing hot–dry–windy events threaten wheat yields in China, with significant yield losses linked to high-temperature, low-humidity conditions. Analysis of extensive yield and climate data reveals worsening sensitivity trends, emphasizing the need for adaptive strategies in agricultural practices.

items.title: When conflict with industrial fishing threatens coastal communities
items.abstract: We developed a global index to identify small-scale fishing communities that are most vulnerable to conflict with industrial fleets. Areas with highest vulnerability, where fishing supports many livelihoods and essential needs, were found to be concentrated in Africa and Asia. Our results highlight priorities for equitable fisheries governance.

items.title: Selective extraction of phenolic compounds from barley waste using deep eutectic solvents
items.abstract: In this study, the development of an ultrasound method for extraction of phenolic compounds from barley waste using acidic deep eutectic solvents (UAE-DES) was investigated. Optimization of the extraction parameters, which include extraction time, temperature, and ultrasound power (UP), was performed using the One-Factor-at-a-Time (OFAT) experimental design, followed by HPLC-PDA for determination of total quantified phenolic content (TQPC). In addition, the influence of water addition on TQPC was evaluated. The Maximum TQPC obtained was 5.78 mg/g using ChCl: formic acid at a molar ratio (1:2) and optimal conditions of (70 °C, 30 min, 80% UP, 10% water), and 4.67 mg/g, using ChCl: tartaric acid at a molar ratio (1:2) and optimal conditions of (70 °C, 25 min, 100% UP, and 20% water). The obtained TQPC was 5- and 4-fold higher in comparison with 70% methanol and 70% ethanol extraction. LC–MS-qTOF analysis of DES extracts revealed diverse phenolic compounds, while the concentration range of compounds obtained was as follows: ferulic acid (0.86–2.47 mg/g), catechin (0.12–2.16 mg/g), p-coumaric acid (0.12–0.32 mg/g), naringenin (0.54–0.86 mg/g), and apigenin (0.15–0.91 mg/g). SEM analysis confirmed enhanced accessibility of lignocellulose in DES-treated samples. The sustainability of UAE-DES extraction was assessed using AGREE, AGREEprep, CACI, BAGI, and CaFRI green tools. The grade assessment of each tool resulted in scores: 0.63 for AGREE, 0.57 for AGREEprep, 65 for CACI, 82.5 for BAGI, and 72 for CaFRI, indicating a greener extraction performance of UAE-DES in comparison with …

items.title: The assessment of gastric myoelectrical activity between different stomach regions based on three-channel electrogastrogram signals: a pilot study
items.abstract: IntroductionPrevious studies have widely used surface electrogastrogram (EGG) signals to non-invasively evaluate gastric motility. However, it focused only on the assessment of electrical activity in a certain stomach region and lacked the analysis of interactions between different gastric regions. In the study, we aimed to assess the correlations of myoelectrical activity between distinct stomach areas using functional connectivity (FC) methods by three-channel EGG for the first time.MethodsThe study contained 20 healthy subjects and the dataset for each subject consisted of two three-channel EGG signals (labeled as CH1, CH2 and CH3; CH1 projected onto the region of lesser curvature, CH3 projected onto the region of greater curvature, and CH2 positioned the region between CH1 and CH3) with a sampling rate of 2 Hz acquired from three locations of stomach during a 20-minute period of fasting and postprandial states respectively. Firstly, the EGG signals were band-pass filtered into three slow wave (SW) bands by finite impulse response (FIR) filter, namely bradygastria (0.017-0.033 Hz), normogastria (0.033-0.067 Hz) and tachygastria (0.067-0.15 Hz). Secondly, we employed four FC algorithms (i.e. Spearman correlation coefficient (SCC), phase lag index (PLI), mutual information (MI) and coherence (Coh)) to calculate the connection strength of each pair of gastric areas. Finally, the FC strength between fasting and postprandial conditions for all subjects or the normal weight (NW) or overweight (OW) people and between the NW and OW groups for both fasting and postprandial states…

items.title: Quality evaluation of a traditional Chinese medicine compound preparation containing Rhodiola rosea, Astragalus membranaceus, and Carthamus tinctorius
items.abstract: ObjectiveWe aim to improve the quality control of Rhodiola rosea, Astragalus membranaceus, and Carthamus tinctorius capsules (RAC capsule) from the aspects of thin-layer chromatography (TLC) and high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), respectively, and the established quality control methods are suitable for their popularization and application in large-scale production.MethodsA TLC method was established for the identification of R. rosea, A. membranaceus, and C. tinctorius in RAC capsules. A HPLC method with gradient elution and UV detection was established for simultaneous determination of salidroside, tyrosol, hydroxysafflor yellow A (HSYA), anhydrosafflor yellow B (ASYB), and rhodiolin.ResultsThe TLC chromatograms showed distinct and reproducible spots for the RAC capsule samples at positions consistent with those of the corresponding reference crude drugs, while no interfering spots were observed in the negative control samples. The HPLC method demonstrated excellent linearity (R2 > 0.9991) for all five analytes within their respective concentration ranges with precision, stability, and repeatability; RSDs all below 2%; and average recoveries ranging from 95.07% to 105.61%.ConclusionThe developed TLC and HPLC methods are specific, accurate, and robust, providing a reliable quality control strategy for RAC capsules. The study supports the standardization of this herbal capsule formulation and establishes a foundation for further pharmacological research and clinical investigations.

items.title: Complementary techniques for investigating the molecular dynamics of uncrystallized water
items.abstract: Uncrystallized water (UCW) refers to the fraction of water in hydrated materials that remains uncrystallized upon cooling. Rather than forming bulk ice, this water retains molecular mobility even below the nominal freezing point. In polymers and proteins, UCW includes strongly bound water associated with specific functional groups and more weakly confined water residing in nanoscale environments. As a result, it plays an important role in mechanical behavior, structural stability, and biological function. Because UCW is heterogeneous, no single technique can fully capture its properties, and multiple complementary methods are required. This review highlights how dielectric spectroscopy (DS), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), neutron scattering, particularly quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS), and terahertz and infrared spectroscopies each probe different aspects of UCW across distinct time and different sample sizes. We outline what each technique measures, the models commonly used to interpret the data, and how combining these approaches helps distinguish between “free,” “bound,” and “non-freezable” water. Studies that apply multiple methods to the same samples, with consistent control of hydration and temperature, are essential for developing a coherent and quantitative picture of UCW. This integrated approach is also key to translating UCW behavior into practical design principles for cryopreservation, pharmaceutical freezing, and biomaterials. Importantly, complementarity arises from differences in timescale and the distinct …

items.title: Highly sensitive detection of soybean-derived DNA in soy sauce using an integrated PCR-CRISPR/Cas12a nucleic acid detection platform
items.abstract: IntroductionSoy sauce is a traditional fermented condiment with widespread global consumption, and its authenticity depends on the requisite use of soybeans as a primary ingredient. However, for economic gain, soybean has been partially or completely substituted with cheaper materials, including other legumes such as pea or peanut, or non‐soybean nitrogen sources such as acid‐hydrolysed animal protein derived from feathers or hair. Such practices constitute economic fraud and labelling violations and may introduce undeclared allergens, raising legitimate concerns regarding food safety and consumer trust. Conventional DNA‐based detection techniques are often hindered by DNA fragmentation and the presence of PCR inhibitors in the complex, fermented matrix, leading to compromised sensitivity and reliability.MethodsTo overcome these limitations, we developed a novel nucleic acid detection platform that synergistically combines target pre‐amplification via polymerase chain reaction (PCR) with highly specific sequence recognition and signal amplification utilizing the CRISPR/Cas12a system.ResultsThis integrated approach achieved a detection limit of 10 femtomolar (fM) for a synthetic Le1 target DNA standard, which compares favourably with many existing methods. The practical applicability of this assay was preliminarily evaluated on 22 commercially available soy sauce samples from various markets.Discussion This study establishes a sensitive and reproducible endpoint‐fluorescence tool for the detection of soybean‐derived DNA. The assay holds promise for routine food authenticatio…

items.title: Comparative compositional analysis and orthogonal GC-MS screening of pristine and expired Chyavanaprasha Lehya: a food-matrix pilot study
items.abstract: BackgroundChyavanaprasha Lehya is a widely recognized polyherbal Ayurvedic nutraceutical and a complex semisolid food matrix. Whether it retains product safety while undergoing compositional degradation beyond its shelf life remains unknown. This question is particularly relevant because the Ayurvedic concept of Saviryata Avadhi, denoting a 1-year period of optimal potency, and the 3-year regulatory shelf life may represent distinct constructs. This pilot investigation examined the relationship between post-expiration product safety and matrix-level compositional integrity across multiple analytical domains.MethodologyThis study compared one pristine market sample with an 8-month post-expiration counterpart using a panel of microbial assessment, organoleptic examination, physicochemical parameters, total protein, total carbohydrate, total phenolic content, total flavonoid content, and DPPH radical-scavenging capacity, together with orthogonal dual-column (HP-5ms/DB-WAX) electron ionization gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (EI GC-MS). Compounds tentatively identified by NIST library matching were classified according to the ChemOnt taxonomy. Quantitative assays were performed in technical triplicate. Nutritional and phytochemical parameters were compared using Welch’s t-tests with Bonferroni correction (α = 0.0125), while DPPH IC50 was evaluated separately at α = 0.05.ResultsBoth samples met the microbial acceptance criteria and remained organoleptically similar, although the expired sample showed modest physicochemical deviations, including a reduced water-soluble extra…

items.title: A data-driven predictive system for shellfish biotoxin risk assessment
items.abstract: Diarrhetic shellfish poisoning (DSP) toxins pose a major threat to the aquaculture industry and public health. Traditional monitoring methods suffer from delays and high costs, and intelligent early warning systems are urgently needed. The study utilised machine learning to predict shellfish biotoxin levels in shellfish by integrating multiple data sources, including phytoplankton monitoring, climatic variables, and historical toxin records. Data from seven shellfish production areas in Northern Ireland from 2011 to 2021, covering DSP-OA + dinophysistoxins and AZAs toxin concentrations, seven phytoplankton taxa or taxonomic groups, and three climatic variables was used to inform the model. Using the Lale Machine learning framework, the study constructed 42 initial modelling scenarios across regions, shellfish species, and toxin combinations. SHAP analyses quantified feature contributions and identified the main predictors across the retained scenarios. After data filtering and performance screening, model performance varied across the region-species combinations. The final regression models showed limited predictive performance, while the classification models showed stronger performance for the two evaluated region-species combinations, Belfast mussels and Dundrum mussels, with F1 scores of 0.766 and 0.950. The results of the study show predictive potential for toxin occurrence at the next sampling occasion, although further validation is required before operational early-warning application.

items.title: Effect of pumpkin pulp (Cucurbita maxima) pigments as natural colorants in ice cream: extraction efficiency, bioactive compounds and sensory acceptance
items.abstract: IntroductionPumpkin (Cucurbita maxima) pulp is a promising source of natural pigments with potential applications as food colorants. This study evaluated three extraction methods and the sensory acceptance of pumpkin-derived pigments in ice cream.MethodsMaceration, Soxhlet extraction, and supercritical CO2 extraction were compared in terms of extraction yield, total carotenoid and flavonoid contents, and DPPH antioxidant activity expressed as IC50. Analytical determinations were performed in triplicate. Extraction methods were compared using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey’s HSD test. The Soxhlet extract was selected for ice cream formulation, which was evaluated by 100 untrained adult panelists using a five-point hedonic scale. Sensory data were analyzed using the Kruskal–Wallis test followed by Dunn–Bonferroni comparisons.ResultsSupercritical CO2 extraction resulted in the highest carotenoid content (315.22 ± 0.01 mg kg−1) and total flavonoid content (1099.08 ± 0.04 mg QE kg−1 extract). Soxhlet extraction achieved the highest extraction yield (22.72 ± 0.33%) and the lowest IC50 value (1.06 ± 0.035 mg/mL). The formulation containing 600 mg of extract per 600 g of ice cream (Z3) showed the highest color acceptance. Significant differences were detected for color (p < 0.05), but not for odor, flavor, or texture (p > 0.05).DiscussionThe extraction method affected both extraction yield and the measured characteristics of the pumpkin extracts. The results support the potential of pumpkin-derived pigments as natural food colorants, although further work is needed to evaluate the…

items.title: Molecular dinitrogen anions pave the way for low-temperature ammonia synthesis
items.abstract: While ammonia (NH₃) is best known for its role in fertilizer production, it is attracting attention as a carbon-free hydrogen carrier, potentially offering a practical way to store and transport clean fuel. Despite this promise, NH₃ synthesis still depends on high-temperature, high-pressure processes that are difficult to scale up sustainably. The reason behind this is the extremely strong bond between nitrogen atoms in nitrogen gas (N₂), which requires a lot of energy to break.

items.title: Chemists develop AI tool to convert human ingenuity into life-enhancing enzymes
items.abstract: Many have voiced concerns that artificial intelligence will take jobs away from humans. But assistant professor of chemistry Zhongyue (John) Yang, along with his former doctoral student Qianzhen Shao (now a postdoc at Stanford) and other team members, has created an AI tool that aims to elevate the work that scientists do—not replace them.

items.title: 'Molecular armor' can trap shape-matched planar molecules
items.abstract: A research team has designed and synthesized a molecular cage with an internal cavity by connecting two curved π-conjugated molecules face-to-face at three points.

items.title: Novel chemical reaction expands options for building DNA-encoded libraries
items.abstract: Finding new drugs requires screening vast numbers of compounds to identify those that interact with a biological target. DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) help researchers explore these large collections by attaching a short DNA sequence to each molecule, acting as a molecular barcode that allows compounds with promising properties to be identified.

items.title: Scientists discover a plastic-eating “Pac-Man” enzyme with a surprising secret
items.abstract: Scientists have discovered a remarkable “Pac-Man enzyme” that helps bacteria devour certain types of plastic and may offer new hope in the fight against plastic pollution. Researchers found that several biodegradable plastics completely broke down in soil within about a year, while conventional plastic remained largely unchanged.

items.title: Scientists discover why a 100-year-old mushroom disease won't go away
items.abstract: Scientists have uncovered a surprising secret behind a mushroom disease that has frustrated growers for more than a century: It involves more than 17 species of harmful bacteria, not just one. The discovery could explain why treatments have struggled to stop the disease and open the door to more effective, eco-friendly solutions.

items.title: The “glue” holding your cells together has a surprising second job
items.abstract: Scientists have discovered that E-cadherin, a protein best known as the “glue” holding cells and tissues together, has a surprising second job: helping epithelial cells swallow nearby dead cells. Using live zebrafish and mouse embryos, researchers found that cells can dramatically reshape their lower surfaces to engulf cellular debris while keeping their upper surfaces stable, allowing protective barriers to remain sealed.

items.title: Scientists find evidence for two origins of life on Earth
items.abstract: Scientists probing life’s deepest origins have uncovered evidence that the first free-living cells may have emerged not once, but twice. The findings suggest a striking possibility: life may share one ancient genetic code, yet have undergone two separate transitions into free-living existence.

items.title: Scientists discover new Alzheimer’s drug that repairs DNA damage and reduces brain inflammation
items.abstract: Scientists have discovered that a drug originally developed for spinal cord injuries can tackle several key features of Alzheimer’s disease, including DNA damage and inflammation. Already tested for initial safety in humans, the experimental treatment could offer a faster path toward therapies that target the disease at its roots.

items.title: Experts say high blood pressure guidelines are missing half the equation
items.abstract: Scientists are calling for a major rethink of how we manage high blood pressure, suggesting that eating more potassium could be just as important as cutting back on salt. A new report finds that combining increased potassium intake with reduced sodium consumption may offer greater benefits for blood pressure control than sodium reduction alone.

items.title: Drinking tea may help protect your heart, but there’s a surprising catch
items.abstract: A massive study of nearly 486,000 adults found that regularly drinking tea was associated with an 11% lower risk of heart and blood vessel diseases. The lowest risk was linked to drinking roughly six to eight cups per day, with black tea showing more consistent benefits than green tea.

items.title: Even moderate drinking linked to cancer and early death, major study finds
items.abstract: A major new study challenges the idea that moderate drinking is safe, finding that even relatively small amounts of alcohol increase the risk of cancer, heart disease, and premature death. Researchers found no overall health benefits from drinking and warn that consuming more than one alcoholic beverage per day can significantly increase long-term health risks.

items.title: CONUT score at ICU discharge predicts long-term all-cause mortality risk in elderly survivors of pneumonia-induced sepsis
items.abstract: Background and objectivesAlthough the Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score has been confirmed to be associated with short-term mortality in intensive care unit (ICU) patients with sepsis, evidence on long-term post-ICU mortality remains limited. This study assessed its prognostic performance for long-term all-cause mortality in elderly survivors of pneumonia-induced sepsis and compared it with several immunoinflammatory nutritional indices.MethodsFrom the initial pool of 620 candidates, we screened 510 first-episode sepsis survivors with no sepsis recurrence more than 3 months after ICU discharge. We subsequently established a multicenter ambispective longitudinal cohort of 461 eligible participants for prospective follow-up, with a median follow-up period of 36 months. Using a complete-case approach with ICU discharge as time zero, we assessed the association between CONUT and mortality across the CONUT score tertiles: T1 (score 0–3, n = 162), T2 (4–6, n = 172), and T3 (7–12, n = 127). Sensitivity analyses were conducted to address selection, immortal-time, and landmark biases.ResultsLong-term risk of all-cause mortality increased stepwise across CONUT tertiles (24.07% vs. 37.21% vs. 58.27%; p < 0.0001). Kaplan–Meier analysis demonstrated significantly lower survival in patients with higher CONUT scores (log-rank, p < 0.0001). Multivariable Cox regression (Model III) revealed that one tertile increase in CONUT was associated with a 23.3% higher mortality risk (hazard ratio (HR) = 1.233, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.004–1.515; p for trend = 0.036), while the hig…

items.title: Functional food intervention alleviates cognitive impairment by reshaping the gut microbiota and restoring propionate levels: evidence from edible bird’s nest supplementation
items.abstract: IntroductionAging-related cognitive decline is closely associated with synaptic dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and alterations in gut microbial homeostasis. Edible bird’s nest (EBN), a glycoprotein-rich functional food, has attracted attention for its potential neuroprotective effects. However, whether EBN has an ameliorative effect on aging-related cognitive impairment remains unclear. This study evaluated the effects of EBN supplementation on memory impairment in a D-galactose (D-gal) -induced aging model and explored the potential mechanisms.MethodsMice were subjected to chronic D-gal administration and treated with low or high-dose EBN or sialic acid (SA). Spatial learning and memory were assessed using the Morris water maze. Hippocampal neuronal morphology, dendritic spine density, synaptic marker expression, glial activation, and inflammatory cytokines were evaluated. Gut microbial composition was analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, while fecal short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) were quantified by gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS). Correlation analysis was performed to examine the association between gut microbial taxa and SCFA levels.ResultsD-gal treatment induced marked cognitive impairment in mice, as reflected by reduced spatial memory performance, decreased hippocampal dendritic spine density, and diminished expression of synaptic markers including Bdnf (brain-derived neurotrophic factor), Dlg4 (postsynaptic density protein 95), and Syp (synaptophysin). In contrast, EBN supplementation, particularly at the higher dose, significantly improved spatial…

items.title: Gestational weight gain trajectories and outcome-informed reference ranges among women with gestational diabetes: a BMI-stratified cohort study
items.abstract: BackgroundGestational weight gain (GWG) is an important modifiable component of nutritional management in gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), but stage-specific patterns and appropriate total GWG ranges across pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI) categories remain uncertain. This study aimed to characterize gestational-age-specific GWG trajectories and stage-specific patterns in relation to GDM diagnosis based on oral glucose tolerance testing (OGTT), derive BMI-stratified local reference ranges for total GWG, and internally compare their risk-stratification performance with national recommendations.Materials and methodsThis retrospective cohort study included 9,008 women with singleton pregnancies complicated by GDM who delivered between February 2021 and December 2025. Population-level centile curves characterized GWG patterns, and the interquartile range of total GWG among women without adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs) defined the locally derived, outcome-informed empirical reference range (LOC). Generalized additive models and multivariable logistic regression assessed associations between GWG and APOs. LOC and National Health Commission (NHC) discrimination was internally evaluated using 2,000 bootstrap resamples with optimism correction.ResultsGWG showed stage- and BMI-specific patterns, increasing more rapidly before OGTT-based diagnosis and generally slowing thereafter. Post-diagnosis rates approached NHC recommendations among underweight or normal-weight women but remained relatively high among overweight or obese women. The LOC ranges were 11.0–15.0, 9.2–14.0, 7.…

items.title: Opportunities and limitations of image analysis-based microplastic quantification and characterization in a hydrological context
items.abstract: Precise characterization of microplastic morphology and size distribution is essential for understanding particle mobility through porous media, since particle size and morphology strongly influence filtration, retention, and transport behavior. Image analysis has been investigated as a cost-effective and efficient way to quantify and measure polydisperse environmental microplastics, but it has yet to be proven effective for use in hydrological studies. In this study, three common image-analysis workflows were evaluated to quantify concentrations and size distributions of Nile Red-stained microplastics in laboratory transport studies. Filter images were captured using (1) a digital single-lens reflex camera; or (2) a stereomicroscope, both as random frames or as stitched full-filter images. Automated particle counts were compared to manual counts from various dilutions, based on panoramic full-filter images. Then, a controlled sand column experiment was conducted as proof-of-concept to evaluate method performance under advective transport conditions. All imaging approaches exhibited concentration-dependent sensitivity, with high particle densities causing quantification and sizing errors due to particle overlap (coincidence) and fluorescence halo effects. Stitched full-filter stereomicroscopic images were deemed too time-consuming for use in high-throughput hydrological studies, but DSLR photography and random frame-stereomicroscopy identified comparable breakthrough timing and mobility trends. Differences in particle recovery and relative concentration magnitudes were driv…

items.title: Phosphorus in Balance: Evaluating the Costs and Benefits of a Circular Economy Approach
items.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive cost-benefit analysis of producing alternative phosphorus (P) fertilizers from recycled water treatment residuals (Fe-WTR) and cowshed effluents. The cost-benefit values of Fe-WTR are compared to the net costs of recycling P using a synthetic adsorbent (commonly used practice-layered double hydroxide, P-LDH) and the costs of commercial fertilizers. Dairy wastewater is used as a source of P. The cost of 1 ton P using the Fe-WTR process is €329. In contrast, synthetic adsorbents (P-LDH) incur significantly higher costs, amounting to €3329 per ton, underscoring the economic advantage of utilizing waste-derived materials. Adopting Fe-WTR fertilizer not only offers substantial cost savings by avoiding landfill fees (€40 per ton) and wastewater discharge fines (€500 per ton) but also reduces environmental impacts when compared to the use of commercial P fertilizers (non-recycled P). The Fe-WTR method mitigates eutrophication and pollution, presenting the dual benefit of cost-effectiveness and environmental protection, which exceeds the common P recycling practice (LDH). Our conclusions are based on production processes in Israel and compared to previous cost estimations at the world level, assessing the potential gain from such circular production of P globally. Recycling P from waste streams can be economically viable and environmentally preferable at small and large economic scales, supporting global sustainability goals.
items.authors: H. E. Ganem, I. Zohar, M. Litaor et al.

items.title: The impact of alternative recycled and synthetic phosphorus sources on plant growth and responses, soil interactions and sustainable agriculture - lettuce (Lactuca sativa) as a case model.
items.abstract: This research assesses the efficacy of two phosphorus (P) adsorbents as alternative fertilizers in promoting lettuce growth. A synthetic Mg/Al-layered double hydroxide (LDH) and an iron-based recycled water treatment residual (Fe-WTR), both enriched with P from dairy wastewater and added at three dosage levels. We hypothesized that the adsorbents' physicochemical nature will overshadow the biological efforts in the plant ecosystem to increase P solubility, impacting plant growth, nutritional composition, and metabolite profiles. Fe-WTR significantly enhanced lettuce biomass compared to LDH. Yet, elemental analysis revealed higher or equal P concentrations in the low-biomass LDH plants relative to other treatments. Phosphorus uptake appears to influence the assimilation of other nutrients that divided into two groups: calcium, magnesium, zinc, and copper with notable correlations to P and nitrogen, iron, aluminum, vanadium and manganese with low correlations to P. Conversely, P retained poor correlation with most metabolites whereas iron showed a higher correlation with numerous metabolites. Analysis of metabolites, encompassing carbohydrates, the Krebs cycle, amino acids, nucleic acids, and stress and regulatory pathways, revealed diminished levels in the LDH treatments. Overall, carbon assimilation (plant growth) was more effectively predicted by soil P availability (adsorbent type and dose) rather than by cellular P concentration, suggesting root signaling was at play, influencing carbohydrate translocation to the roots. items.title: Biogeochemical impacts on soil phosphorus and other macro- and micro elements solubility, ratios and forms during heatwaves
items.abstract: Increased frequency and amplitude of extreme heat events can affect soil temperature, and biogeochemical processes. High temperatures may have contradicting geochemical and biological effects on essential elements solubility and forms. Endothermic behavior of minerals and oxides results in decreased solubility with increased temperature, while bio-mineralization is stimulated in response to high temperature. To elucidate heatwave impacts on soil biogeochemical processes, we performed a controlled soil incubation experiment and a field survey. Wet and dry alluvial soil sets were incubated at background temperature (33°C) for two weeks and then, a sequence of three heat events was induced (41°C/33°C alternations, five days each) followed by two short events of extreme heat (48°C for two days). Most soil indices changed trends after about 25-30 days. At the first part of the period, P, Al, Fe appeared to reflect endothermic behavior of (hydr)oxides and minerals in the dry soil (i.e., sorbed P was likely dependent on Fe (hydr)oxides dissolution), while trends of Fe/Al in the wet soil followed the dissolved organic C trend. Phosphatases enzymatic activities fluctuated positively with temperature, emphasizing the activity of residual extracellular enzymes sorbed to soil particles (dry soil) in addition to living cells excreted enzymes (wet soil). items.title: Dictated cell adhesion and migration using microfluidic-controlled synthetic hydrogels exhibiting programmable viscoelasticities.
items.abstract: Mechanosensing interactions between the extracellular matrix (ECM) and the intracellular cytoskeleton are fundamental to cellular functions such as motility, proliferation, and adhesion, driven by the dynamic, bidirectional, tension-regulated maturation of focal adhesion (FA) sites. We demonstrate that native mechanosensing interactions and their downstream functions are precisely controlled using synthetic hydrogels. We introduce a microfluidic-assisted synthesis of imine-crosslinked hyaluronic acid-gelatin copolymer hydrogels (HAG), enabling controlled, predefined gradient viscoelasticity. Specifically, three native tissues (muscle, epidermis, and cartilage)-mimicking HAG hydrogels were prepared, matching their effective Young's modulus (Ymod) and stress relaxation time (τ1/2). Enhanced cell spreading and directional cell migration are observed, with a preference for substrates with tissue-matching viscoelasticity. These mechanosensing reactions are confirmed by traction force microscopy, revealing a tight correlation between native tissue mechano-properties and the hydrogel viscoelastic parameters. We demonstrate that the signaling efficacies of the FAK and associated YAP/TAZ pathways, central regulators of FA formation and cell migration, are tuned by substrate tissue-matching viscoelasticity. We implement these preprogrammed viscoelastic gradient hydrogels as spatiotemporal cell-separation matrices, enabling viscoelasticity-driven migration of binary cell mixtures. items.title: Redox- and Photo-Responsive Fe3+/2+-Cross-Linked Carboxymethyl Cellulose Methacrylate Dissipative Gels: Synthesis and Applications
items.abstract: The synthesis of redox-active Fe3+-cross-linked carboxymethyl cellulose methacrylate cryogels (Fe 3+ -CMCMA), revealing switchable, transient, dissipative stiffness properties, is introduced. The switchable, transient functions are triggered by ascorbate-mediated reduction of the high-stiffness gel to the lower-stiffness Fe2+-CMCMA gel, and the concomitant aerobic oxidation of the Fe2+-CMCMA to the Fe3+-CMCMA gel state. Alternatively, integration of native photosynthetic photosystem-I (PS-I) into the cryogel matrix allows the photosensitized reduction of the Fe3+-CMCMA cryogel to the lower stiffness state Fe2+-CMCMA, and the concomitant, temporal, aerobic recovery of Fe2+-CMCMA to the high-stiffness Fe3+-CMCMA gel. The transient dissipative stiffness of the Fe3+/2+-CMCMA cryogel is characterized by temporal rheometry, dynamic stretching stress–strain experiments, XPS, and SEM imaging. The transient chemical/light-triggered stiffness functions of the Fe3+/2+-CMCMA, or PS-I-integrated Fe3+/2+-CMCMA gels are applied to develop transient self-healing matrices, and frameworks for cyclic, transient release of loads integrated in the gel matrices. This is exemplified by the ascorbate/light-induced cyclic transient release of tetramethyl rhodamine-dextran (TMR-D), insulin, and the anti-VEGF aptamer loads. In addition, the stimuli-responsive Fe3+/2+-CMCMA cryogel is used to construct a bilayer-soft-robotic bending device. items.title: Chemical and Photochemical-Driven Dissipative Fe3+/Fe2+-Ion Cross-Linked Carboxymethyl Cellulose Gels Operating Under Aerobic Conditions: Applications for Transient Controlled Release and Mechanical Actuation
items.abstract: A Fe3+-ion cross-linked carboxymethyl cellulose, Fe3+-CMC, redox-active gel exhibiting dissipative, transient stiffness properties is introduced. Chemical or photosensitized reduction of the higher-stiffness Fe3+-CMC to the lower-stiffness Fe2+-CMC gel, accompanied by the aerobic reoxidation of the Fe2+-CMC matrix, leads to the dissipative, transient stiffness, functional matrix. The light-induced, temporal, transient release of a load (Texas red dextran) and the light-triggered, transient mechanical bending of a poly-N-isopropylacrylamide (p-NIPAM)/Fe3+-CMC bilayer construct are introduced, thus demonstrating the potential use of the dissipative Fe3+-CMC gel for controlled drug release or soft robotic applications.

items.title: Stimuli-Responsive DNA-Based Hydrogels on Surfaces for Switchable Bioelectrocatalysis and Controlled Release of Loads
items.abstract: The assembly of enzyme [glucose oxidase (GOx)]-loaded stimuli-responsive DNA-based hydrogels on electrode surfaces, and the triggered control over the stiffness of the hydrogels, provides a means to switch the bioelectrocatalytic functions of the hydrogels. One system includes the assembly of GOx-loaded, pH-responsive, hydrogel matrices cross-linked by two cooperative nucleic acid motives comprising permanent duplex nucleic acids and “caged” i-motif pH-responsive duplexes. Bioelectrocatalyzed oxidation of glucose leads to the formation of gluconic acid that acidifies the hydrogel resulting in the separation of the i-motif constituents and lowering the hydrogel stiffness. Loading of the hydrogel matrices with insulin results in the potential-triggered, glucose concentration-controlled, switchable release of insulin from the hydrogel-modified electrodes. The switchable bioelectrocatalyzed release of insulin is demonstrated in the presence of ferrocenemethanol as a diffusional electron mediator or by applying an electrically wired integrated matrix that includes ferrocenyl-modified GOx embedded in the hydrogel. The second GOx-loaded, stimuli-responsive, DNA-based hydrogel matrix associated with the electrode includes a polyacrylamide hydrogel cooperatively cross-linked by duplex nucleic acids and “caged” G-quadruplex-responsive duplexes. The hydrogel matrix undergoes K+-ions/crown ether-triggered stiffness changes by the cyclic K+-ion-stimulated formation of G-quadruplexes (lower stiffness) and the crown ether-induced separation of the G-quadruplexes (higher stiffness). items.title: Stiffness‐Switchable, Biocatalytic pH‐Responsive DNA‐Functionalized Polyacrylamide Cryogels and their Mechanical Applications
items.abstract: The large‐pore interconnected channels in cryogels, allow convectional flow and rapid mass‐transport of solute constituents between the solution and cryogel polymer framework, as compared to slower, diffusionally‐controlled mass‐transport in small‐pore hydrogels. These features are applied to develop enzyme‐loaded polyacrylamide (pAAm) cryogels, and glucose oxidase (GOx)‐loaded pH‐responsive DNA‐based pAAm cryogels, revealing enhanced biocatalytic transformations, enhanced temporal stiffness changes, and mechanical bending functions, as compared to analog hydrogels. DNA‐based pAAm cryogel/hydrogel matrices, revealing pH‐switchable stiffness properties through reversible reconfiguration of DNA‐bridging units into i‐motif structures, are introduced. Enhanced switchable stiffness changes of DNA‐based pAAm cryogels, as compared to analog hydrogels, are demonstrated upon subjecting the cryogel/hydrogel matrices to auxiliary pH‐changes, or by integration of GOx into the frameworks, and driving pH‐changes through GOx‐catalyzed aerobic oxidation of glucose to gluconic acid. Enhanced stiffness changes of pAAm cryogels represent a major advance to control the mechanical properties of cryogels and are attributed to the convectionally‐controlled mass‐transport in the cryogel matrices. Moreover, bilayer constructs consisting of poly‐N‐isopropylacrylamide (pNIPAM) cryogels and pH‐responsive DNA‐based pAAm cryogel or hydrogel structures are constructed.
